row_statement: Identify the people who created a dataset.
statement: Identify the authors of a dataset.

row_statement: Describe the origin and processing history of data.
statement: Describe the lineage of a dataset.
notes: The paper: "Points (2) (data lineage) and (5) (input data) are already supported by DCAT-AP".

row_statement: Give prospective users practical guidance on using a dataset.
statement: Give potential data consumers information on how to use the data (usage notes).

row_statement: Connect datasets to associated scientific publications.
statement: Link a dataset to scientific publications about it.

row_statement: Identify source datasets used in producing a dataset.
statement: Link a dataset to its input data (the data used to create it).
notes: The paper: "Points (2) (data lineage) and (5) (input data) are already supported by DCAT-AP".

row_statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
statement: Use persistent identifiers for dataset authors and input data, so datasets can be reliably filtered and linked by them.
applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.
notes: Context: filtering datasets by authors or input data; JRC datasets already have persistent URIs and ORCIDs are used for authors.

row_statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
statement: Encode identifiers as HTTP URIs wherever possible.
applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.

row_statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
statement: Distinguish primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.
notes: Met by the base: dct:identifier for primary and adms:identifier for alternative identifiers.

row_statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.

applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.

row_statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.

notes: Met by the base (adms:Identifier carries the scheme); the paper questions this modelling because such identifiers are of little use for linking.

row_statement: Express the roles that agents play for a dataset beyond publisher and contact point, consistently across catalogues.

applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.

row_statement: Indicate when a distribution gives access through a service or API rather than to the data itself, and describe the service interface with the query parameters needed to select data.

applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.
notes: dct:type, not a distribution property in DCAT-AP 1.1, used on the distribution.

applicability: Within the cited source scope; not an assertion of universal applicability.
notes: Claude v2 had only "which service standard it follows"; completed from PR #45.
